title: Nuevo Laredo hunting season projected to bring in nearly $20 million
excerpt: Nuevo Laredo's 2026-27 hunting season opens Nov. 20, with officials projecting nearly $20 million in economic activity — up 10 percent from last year — as more than 4,300 hunters head to the region's ranches.
content:
Nuevo Laredo is gearing up for a hunting season that local officials say could bring nearly $20 million into the region, according to Central de Noticias Tamaulipas.

The 2026-27 hunting season officially opens Thursday, Nov. 20. The city government and hunting-sector groups project an economic impact of about $20 million, roughly 10 percent more than the $18 million recorded during the 2025 season.

Tourism officials expect more than 4,300 hunters to visit the region's wildlife management units this season, topping last year's turnout. About 45 percent of the hunters are expected to come from the United States, following promotion at events such as the Texas Trophy Hunters Extravaganza, according to the city's tourism office.

The draw is the region's white-tailed deer and its hunting infrastructure: more than 700 specialized ranches. "Nuevo Laredo cuenta con ventajas competitivas consolidadas," the city's tourism director, Alfredo Guarneros, said, pointing to the ranches and the genetic quality of the region's white-tailed deer as what makes the border city a reference point for sport hunting.

To make the crossing smoother, an assistance and check-in module has been set up at International Bridge No. 2 in coordination with the National Association of Diversified Wildlife Breeders (ANGADI), where hunters can get help with the temporary import of firearms and vehicles. The visitor reception also involves Mexico's Defense Department, the National Guard, the State Guard, the National Migration Institute and the National Customs Agency of Mexico.

Before the season opens, Nuevo Laredo will hold its traditional hunting parade on Saturday, Nov. 22, starting at the Explanada de la Independencia and ending at the Cultural and Convention Center (CITEV), where officials, ranch owners and hunters will gather.

Sources: Central de Noticias Tamaulipas, Nov. 11, 2026; centralnoticiastamaulipas.com.
